mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi engine typically costs between £2,500 and £4,000, including supply and fit. Rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty. Main dealers often charge significantly more for the same replacement. Used engines are a popular budget alternative, starting from around £500.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of engine failure in a Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early detection of emissions or turbo failures can prevent catastrophic damage to your Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi. Signs include persistent loss of power or the vehicle entering limp mode during acceleration, illumination of the engine management or DPF warning light, and unexplained coolant loss, overheating, or blue/white smoke from the exhaust.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends entirely on the vehicle's current market value and overall condition. For most Mk1 models valued under £5,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement is rarely financially viable. A low-mileage used engine or targeted component repair is almost always the most cost-effective solution for these older examples.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi engine swap typically takes 5 to 7 working days. This includes sourcing the correct engine code (e.g., Q4WA or QXWA), nationwide delivery to your chosen specialist, and physical installation, fluid top-up, and comprehensive road testing.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Q4WA and QXWA Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 2.2-litre Duratorq diesel engines from the same family, producing 175 PS. They share the same fundamental architecture and replacement procedures. The different suffixes typically denote minor production variations, emission standard updates, or specific vehicle trim pairings. Replacement units and repair parts are generally interchangeable across both codes.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.2 TDCi was introduced to the Ford S-Max range, it provided a robust, high-torque Duratorq diesel option, replacing the earlier 2.0 TDCi in higher-spec models and offering superior towing and motorway cruising capabilities for family transport.

milestones.description: Q4WA / QXWA (175 PS) introduced in the Ford S-Max Mk1, offering a significant power bump over the 2.0 TDCi, paired with a 6-speed manual or Powershift automatic transmission.
Minor emissions updates to meet Euro 5 standards, though the core Duratorq 2.2 architecture remained unchanged.
Production of the 2.2 TDCi ceased as the S-Max Mk2 launched, transitioning to the newer 2.0 TDCi and 2.0 EcoBlue architectures.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi is a robust workhorse, but as a high-mileage diesel, it is susceptible to emissions-related component failures and turbocharger wear. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbocharger & Injector Failure - Why the Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi Loses Power
problems.rootCause: High mileage and urban driving lead to DPF clogging, which increases backpressure and strains the turbocharger, while injector seals can leak, causing carbon buildup and eventual turbo or injector failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Injector seal replacement, DPF cleaning, or turbo actuator repair.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before the turbo internals or engine block are damaged.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if turbo failure has sent debris into the engine or caused severe oil starvation.

problems.recommendation: For a Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi showing early DPF or EGR warnings, targeted component repair is the most financially sensible route. However, if the vehicle has suffered catastrophic turbo failure or severe overheating, a reconditioned or rebuilt unit is the most reliable long-term solution, provided the vehicle's overall condition and value justify the investment.

problems.h4: DPF & EGR Clogging - Why the Ford S-Max 2.2 TDCi Suffers in Urban Driving
problems.rootCause: Frequent short journeys prevent the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) from reaching optimal regeneration temperatures, leading to soot accumulation and subsequent EGR valve clogging.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: DPF clean and EGR valve replacement or cleaning.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage clogging before structural engine damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if severe clogging has caused catastrophic engine failure or overheating.
